To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proximity of the soothed to the flame zone is the most important factor influencing its reactivity and radiativity.

multidimensional flame dynamics have a first-order effect in soot formation and that the soot formation and soot–flow interactions in a temporally developing jet flame are qualitatively similar to the soot formation processes in spatially developing jet flames.

soot transport is strongly influenced by the proximity of soot to flame zones and that the flame dynamic effects of local strain and curvature on soot transport are important but that enhanced mixing has a first-order impact on soot transport toward flame zones in a temporally developing jet flame.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fundamental study of turbulent combustion and soot formation and is aimed at developing a better understanding of the physical and chemical processes that govern the formation and evolution of soot in turbulent combustion systems.
the development and application of advanced numerical simulation techniques for the study of complex reacting flows, including turbulent combustion.
the development of a comprehensive soot formation and oxidation model, which is capable of describing the soot evolution in turbulent flames with high fidelity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multidimensional effects are important for soot formation, transport, and oxidation, and should be considered in soot modeling.

multidimensional effects on soot transport in turbulent nonpremixed flames can be significant, and that the soot transport effects are due to the combined effects of flame curvature and strain, and the enhanced turbulent mixing of the fuel and oxidizer.
soot transport in turbulent flames is controlled by flame curvature and flame–flow interaction, which in turn is controlled by the turbulent mixing of fuel–oxidizer streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soot modeling approach is adequate, but that the soot–flow–flame interactions are more complex than anticipated, and that more experimental soot data is needed.
the present results provide a detailed description of the flame–soot interaction and soot transport in a temporaldynamic turbulent jet flame.
soot formation and oxidation in turbulent nonpremixed flames are strongly influenced by the flame dynamic effects of curvature, strain, and mixing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flame dynamics are the key to soot formation and destruction in turbulent nonpremixed flames.
soot transport in turbulent flames is strongly influenced by the flame dynamic structure, which is in turn influenced by the turbulent flow structure, which is influenced by the flame itself.
multidimensional effects are critical to understanding the complex soot formation and oxidation dynamics in turbulent flames.
